sections.body:
A transaction can lock individual rows with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, which blocks other writers of the same rows until the transaction ends. FOR SHARE takes a weaker lock that still allows other readers to share it.

Row locks are recorded in the row itself rather than in shared memory, so locking many rows does not exhaust the lock table.

A deadlock happens when two transactions each wait for a lock the other one holds. The server checks for deadlocks after a transaction has waited for deadlock_timeout, which is 1 second by default.

When a cycle is found, one of the transactions is aborted with an error and the other continues. Applications should retry the aborted transaction and take locks in a consistent order.

Advisory locks have a meaning defined by the application. The server only guarantees that two sessions cannot hold the same advisory lock at once.

Function | Scope |

ledger_advisory_lock | session |

ledger_advisory_xact_lock | transaction |

SELECT ledger_advisory_xact_lock(42);

The default index type is a balanced tree. It supports equality and range comparisons such as less than, greater than and between, and it can return rows already sorted, which avoids a separate sort step.

An inverted index stores, for each word, the list of rows that contain it. It is the index type to use for full-text search and for columns that hold arrays.

Inverted indexes are slower to update than tree indexes, because one new row can add entries to many word lists.

A partial index covers only the rows that satisfy a WHERE clause given when the index is created. It is smaller than a full index and is useful when queries only ever touch a known subset of rows, for example unpaid orders.

CREATE INDEX orders_unpaid ON orders (customer_id) WHERE paid = false;
Ledgerline keeps every table in a set of files made of fixed-size pages. This chapter explains how pages are laid out and how changes are made durable.

Every page is 8 kB. A page starts with a 24-byte header that records the page checksum and the position of free space.

Rows are stored from the end of the page towards the header, while the array of row pointers grows from the header towards the end. When the two meet, the page is full and a new page is allocated.

SELECT page_size, header_bytes
FROM ledger_page_info('orders');

Before a changed page is written to its data file, a record describing the change is appended to the write-ahead log. After a crash, the server replays the log from the last checkpoint to restore every committed change.
A checkpoint flushes all dirty pages to disk so that older log segments can be recycled. By default a checkpoint runs every 5 minutes or when 1 GB of log has been written, whichever comes first.

When archive_mode is on, each completed log segment is handed to archive_command. A segment is only recycled after the command reports success, so a failing archive command makes the log directory grow.
